attribution: Dimensions follow Singapore IMDA's Model AI Governance Framework for Agentic AI (2025). Threat-class ids ASI01-ASI10 are the OWASP Agentic Security Initiative agentic threat taxonomy (© OWASP Foundation, CC-BY-SA-4.0). Questions are paraphrased and reference both sources BY ID only — never verbatim source prose.
disclaimer: This is a self-assessment aid, NOT legal advice. It scores an agent's OPERATIONAL authority (AgentRiskTier); it is not an EU AI Act risk classification, which lives on the AiSystem register entry and is a legal call owned by your counsel.

domains.name: Bounding the risk upfront
domains.description: IMDA dimension 1 — the agent's autonomy, data reach and action reversibility are declared, scoped and capped before it runs.

domains.name: Technical guardrails
domains.description: IMDA dimension 2 — what stands between the agent's intent and the tenant's data: tool allowlists, input and output validation, egress control, blast-radius limits.

domains.name: Human accountability and control
domains.description: IMDA dimension 3 — a named accountable human, approval gates on consequential actions, and a kill switch that actually stops the agent.

domains.name: Traceability, evaluation and response
domains.description: IMDA dimension 4 — every action is attributable and reconstructable, the agent is evaluated before and after deployment, and there is a rehearsed response when it misbehaves.

questions.text: Is the agent's maximum autonomy level a deliberate decision recorded in the register, rather than whatever its credentials happen to permit?
questions.guidance: YES requires that the registered autonomy level was chosen for this agent's job and that no credential can drive it higher.

questions.text: Is the agent's reach into tenant data the narrowest that lets it do its job — and does it stop at the platform boundary unless external egress is genuinely required?
questions.guidance: YES requires an explicit scope decision. An agent granted EXTERNAL_EGRESS 'in case it needs it' is a NO.

questions.text: Have you enumerated the actions this agent can take that CANNOT be undone by the platform, and accepted each one?
questions.guidance: Sending an external notification, publishing a document, telling a third party. YES requires the list to exist and to have been read by the accountable owner.

questions.text: For a third-party or vendor-supplied agent, have you assessed the supplier's own agent-security posture and pinned the version you run?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI08 (agent supply chain). A first-party agent built in-house may answer NA.

questions.text: Is there a written statement of what this agent is NOT permitted to do, distinct from the list of what it is for?
questions.guidance: The out-of-scope list is what an incident review reads first. YES requires it to exist in writing.

questions.text: Is the agent's tool access an explicit allowlist, so that a tool the server offers is not by itself permission to call it?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI02 (tool misuse). YES requires deny-by-default: an ungranted tool is refused server-side.

questions.text: Are untrusted inputs the agent reads — retrieved documents, ticket bodies, web content, other agents' output — treated as data rather than as instructions?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI01 (behavioural manipulation) and ASI04 (context and memory poisoning). YES requires a concrete mechanism, not a prompt asking the model to be careful.

questions.text: Are the agent's outputs validated against a schema or safety check before anything acts on them?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI05 (unexpected code execution) where output feeds a shell, a query, or another system.

questions.text: Does the agent hold its OWN identity and credentials, rather than borrowing a human's session or a shared service account?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI03 (identity and privilege abuse). A borrowed identity makes every action unattributable and every permission the human's.

questions.text: Is there a bound on how much the agent can do in one run — a rate limit, a step budget, or a blast-radius cap on records touched?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI06 (cascading failures). YES requires the bound to be enforced, not documented.

questions.text: If this agent calls or is called by other agents, is that chain bounded and are the other agents themselves registered?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI06 and ASI10. An agent whose peers are unregistered has an unbounded effective surface. NA if the agent works alone.

questions.text: Does a named human own this agent, and would that person be told — and expected to act — if it misbehaved today?
questions.guidance: A vacant or nominal owner is a NO. The register requires an owner; this asks whether the owner is real.

questions.text: Do the agent's consequential actions pass through a human decision before they take effect?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI07 (human-agent trust exploitation) only when the review is real — an approver shown a summary they cannot check is a PARTIALLY at best.

questions.text: Is there a kill switch that stops this agent within one request cycle, and has somebody used it in a drill?
questions.guidance: YES requires both. An untested kill switch is a plan, not a control.

questions.text: Are the humans who review this agent's proposals trained on what it is plausibly wrong about?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI07. Fluent, confident and wrong is the failure mode an untrained approver rubber-stamps.

questions.text: Is every action the agent takes attributable to THIS agent, with enough recorded to reconstruct why it acted?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI09 (insufficient observability). Logs that say a change happened but not which agent made it, or on what basis, are a NO.

questions.text: Can you enumerate every agent running against this tenant, so that an unregistered one would be noticed?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI10 (rogue agents / governance evasion). YES requires the register to be enforced at the credential boundary, not maintained by convention.

questions.text: Was this agent evaluated against adversarial cases — injection through its inputs, tool misuse, escalation attempts — before it was given live authority?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI01, ASI02 and ASI05. A functional test suite is not an adversarial evaluation.

questions.text: Is there a rehearsed response for this agent misbehaving — who is paged, what is revoked, how the actions it took are found and undone?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI09. YES requires the recovery step, not only the stop step.

questions.text: Is the agent monitored in production for behaviour drift after a model, prompt or tool change?
questions.guidance: Covers ASI04 and ASI06. A change that alters behaviour without altering the code is the one nothing else catches.
